questions.q: Which platform aggregates, correlates, and alerts on logs from across the entire organization?
questions.explain: The SIEM is the convergence point for logs: aggregation, correlation, alerting, and archiving.

questions.q: Match each protocol to what it provides.
questions.explain: Each protocol carries a distinct type of data: events, flows, counters, compliance. SCAP is from objective 4.4 (beyond textbooks).

questions.q: A real incident occurred, but no alert was generated. How is this case classified?
questions.explain: False negative = actual malicious activity that went undetected. This is the most dangerous case.

questions.q: Which actions represent proper alert tuning? (Select all that apply)
options: Measuring the impact on alert volume
questions.explain: Tuning is targeted, documented, and measured. Deleting the rule also destroys detection of real attacks.

questions.q: Which mechanism copies traffic from a switch port to a sensor without interrupting traffic flow?
questions.explain: SPAN replicates traffic to an analyzer; unlike a tap, it depends on the switch and can become saturated.

questions.q: Which activity is a prerequisite for multi-source event correlation?
questions.explain: You can only correlate events that have been collected, timestamped, and normalized beforehand.
